# Boomin Full Agent Context

Boomin is programmable distribution infrastructure. It lets customers run partner
distribution — enrollment, approval, referral attribution, coordinated launches,
budgets, measurement, and payouts — without rebuilding email OTP, Instagram OAuth,
approval queues, attribution plumbing, async execution machinery, or scoped
automation credentials.

Docs: https://developers.boomin.ai

## Canonical model

```
Partner            durable identity capable of distributing value
  Partnership      durable brand<->partner relationship (program-independent)
    Enrollment     that partnership's participation in ONE program

Distribution       intent — a coordinated objective. NEVER an execution mode.
  Deployment       execution — one concrete thing running somewhere
    Performance    measurement, recorded against the deployment

Operation          durable async work for EVERY external mutation
Connection         provider identity (owner: partner XOR brand) + per-partnership grants
```

A Distribution is Boomin's PaymentIntent: declare the objective, Boomin fans it
out into Deployments and reports back what actually happened.

Distributions have no `kind` column and no `program` column. `subjects` (event,
offer, resource) are descriptive context only — they never create or constrain a
deployment and are excluded from `plan_hash`.

## Two rails

### Rail 1 — evergreen program, no distribution

The classic referral/affiliate rail. Needs no distribution at all.

1. Create a program, invite partners (`enrollments.create`), approve them.
2. Each approved enrollment gets a program `referral_code` (unique per program).
3. Qualification requirements and tiers evaluate continuously from tracked activity.
4. Rewards and payouts accrue against the program.

Nothing is launched. Nothing is budgeted. Activity is written as program metric
events and feeds qualification and rewards.

```js
const enrollment = await boomin.enrollments.create({ program: "prog_...", email: "creator@example.com" });
await boomin.enrollments.approve(enrollment.id);
// enrollment.referral_code is live. That is the whole rail.
```

### Rail 2 — a distribution layered on top

A time-boxed, funded, measurable push over the same partners.

1. Create a distribution referencing one or more programs.
2. `validate()`, then `launch()`.
3. Boomin creates ONE deployment per eligible enrollment per planned slot, each
   with its OWN attribution instrument, distinct from the program referral code.
4. Conversions route by `deployment_id`, so two distributions sharing an
   enrollment credit separately.
5. A funded budget draws down as rewards are granted; the unconsumed remainder
   is released on cancel or completion.

```js
const distribution = await boomin.distributions.create({
  name: "Spring launch",
  objective: "launch",
  programs: ["prog_..."],
  budget: { mode: "funded", asset: "credit", total: 100000 },
});
await boomin.distributions.validate(distribution.id);
const { operation } = await boomin.distributions.launch(distribution.id);
```

The rails compose. Program activity outside any distribution stays on the program
rail permanently — it is not migrated and it keeps feeding qualification.
Distribution execution that is program-relevant PROJECTS into the program spine.

## Enrollment state — two orthogonal fields

| Field | Values | Moved by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `approval_status` | pending, approved, rejected | approve() / reject() ONLY |
| `status` | active, paused, archived | pause() / resume() ONLY |

Approval commands never touch `status`. Pause/resume never touch
`approval_status`. Rejection is NOT terminal — re-inviting resets approval to
pending, and a rejected enrollment may be approved directly.

`resume` is the canonical verb on every surface. There is no `unpause`.

Approving the first enrollment activates the durable partnership. Partnership
status is `pending` -> `active` -> (`paused`) -> `ended`; `end()` is terminal and
never fires automatically.

## Pausing, money, and event time

Resolved at the event's `occurred_at`, never at ingestion:

| While paused | Links resolve | Attribution | Rewards | Billing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Enrollment paused | yes | continues | STOPS | continues |
| Partnership paused | yes | continues | STOPS | continues |
| Enrollment archived | code retained for history | — | stops | stops |
| Partnership ended | — | — | stops | stops |

Pausing never dodges the active-partner fee while the partner's links still
resolve. `archive` and `partnership.end` are the billing exits.

`partnership.pause` blocks NEW partner deployments across ALL programs, pauses
existing ones via operations, and PRESERVES enrollments and connection grants
untouched so resume is exact.

## Platform API v1 — wire contract

- Base: `https://api.boomin.ai/v1/platform`
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer sk_boomin_live_...`. Bearer-only — no body token, no cookie session.
- Brand: `Boomin-Brand: <id-or-slug>` for multi-brand orgs; default = the org's oldest brand. Webhook endpoints are ORG-scoped, not brand-scoped.
- Updates are POST (Stripe style), never PATCH.
- `Idempotency-Key` on every mutation, including DELETE. Reusing a key with a different body is `idempotency_key_conflict` (409).
- Success bodies are BARE top-level objects.
- Lists: `{"object":"list","data":[...],"has_more":boolean}`. `?limit=` 1-100 (default 20), `?starting_after=<id>`.
- Ids prefixed on output, accepted with or without prefix: `prog_` `ptnr_` `pship_` `enr_` `dist_` `dep_` `conn_` `op_` `evt_` `perf_` `po_` `pob_` `we_`.
- A WRONG prefix for the resource returns that resource's typed 404 — existence is never leaked across tenants.
- Errors: `{"error":{"code","message","param","request_id"}}`. `request_id` is also the `Request-Id` header.
- Auth runs BEFORE id resolution: an unauthenticated probe is always 401, never 404.
- The whole surface sits behind an operator kill switch -> `developer_access_paused` (503).

### The only non-bare responses

```jsonc
// POST /distributions/{id}/launch -> 202. ID STRINGS, never embedded objects.
{ "distribution": "dist_...", "status": "launching", "operation": "op_..." }

// POST /distributions/{id}/pause|resume|cancel  -> 202
// POST /deployments/{id}/pause|resume|cancel    -> 202
{ "id": "dist_...", "object": "distribution", /* … */ "operation": "op_..." }

// webhook_endpoints create/retrieve/update/rotate_secret
{ "webhook_endpoint": { "id": "we_...", /* … */ } }
```

Reads that add a companion field alongside the bare resource:
`distributions.validate` adds `valid` + `errors`; `partnerships.retrieve` adds
`enrollments`; `payouts.batches.retrieve` adds `items`;
`performance.events.create` adds `duplicate` + `projected`;
`payouts.exportCsv` adds `items`, `skipped`, `export_file_key`, `download_url`.

## SDK

```bash
npm install @boomin/sdk
```

```js
import Boomin from "@boomin/sdk";

const boomin = new Boomin(process.env.BOOMIN_SECRET_KEY, {
  baseUrl: "https://api.boomin.ai", // ORIGIN — the SDK appends /v1/platform
  brand: "brand_123",
  maxRetries: 2,
  timeout: 30000,
});
```

fetch + WebCrypto only, zero dependencies, no Node builtins: Node >= 18,
Cloudflare Workers, Bun, Deno, edge.

Per-call RequestOptions is the TRAILING argument of every method:
`{ idempotencyKey, brand, timeout, maxRetries }`. Methods that take a body are
`(id, params, options)`; verbs with no body take `{}` or `null` for params.

Query params are camel->snake converted (`startingAfter` -> `starting_after`).
REQUEST BODIES ARE NOT — send `enabled_events`, `value_minor`, `period_start`,
`referral_code` exactly as the API names them.

Lists resolve one page and are ALSO async-iterable across every page:

```js
const page = await boomin.partnerships.list({ limit: 20 });      // one page
for await (const e of boomin.enrollments.list({ program })) { }  // every page
```

### The 12 clients

- `programs` — `retrieve` `list`; nested `requirements` / `tiers` (create, retrieve, update, list, del) and `connectConfig` / `handoffConfig` (retrieve, update). NOTE: `create`/`update` exist on the client but have NO route in this release.
- `partners` — `retrieve` `list`. NOTE: no `/v1/platform/partners` routes in this release. Read partner identity off `partnerships` (which embeds `partner: {id, name, email}`).
- `partnerships` — `list` `retrieve` `pause` `resume` `end` `updatePermissions`
- `enrollments` — `create` (invite) `retrieve` `list` `approve` `reject` `pause` `resume`
- `distributions` — `create` `retrieve` `update` `list` `validate` `launch` `pause` `resume` `cancel`
- `deployments` — `retrieve` `list`. The pause/resume/cancel ROUTES are live (scope `distributions:write`); SDK methods are not.
- `connections` — `list` `retrieve` `revoke`
- `performance` — `summary` + `events.create`
- `events` — `list` (operational domain-event feed OUT)
- `operations` — `retrieve` `list` `wait`
- `webhooks` — `endpoints.create/retrieve/update/list/del/rotateSecret` + `constructEvent`
- `payouts` — `list` `run` `exportCsv` `connectStatus` + `batches.list/retrieve`

## Distribution lifecycle

```
draft        -> validating                validate()
validating   -> ready                     checks pass
validating   -> draft                     checks fail (errors in `error`)
draft|ready  -> draft                     any update() invalidates validation
ready        -> launching                 launch() -> 202 + operation
launching    -> active                    all deployments live
launching    -> partially_active          some live
launching    -> failed                    ZERO deployments live at terminal launch
launching    -> canceled                  cancel() supersedes the live launch
active|partially_active -> paused         pause()
paused       -> launching                 resume() (re-applies desired state)
active|partially_active -> completed      all deployments terminal
draft|ready|active|partially_active|paused -> canceled   cancel()
```

No `revise()` verb — `update()` in draft|ready with automatic validation
invalidation IS the revision path. No `canceling` status: the distribution
carries the requested lifecycle, operations expose async progress. Program
associations are draft-only.

`validate()` is SYNCHRONOUS in v1. Validation error codes: `program_required`,
`budget_incomplete`, `slot_incomplete` (carries `slot`),
`channel_type_not_yet_supported` (carries `slot`).

Deployment plan (`spec`), all fields optional — the default is one referral-link
slot per approved enrollment:

```js
spec: { plan: { partner: {
  enrollment_policy: "all_approved",
  slots: [{ name: "primary", medium: "referral", channel: "boomin", format: "referral_link" }],
} } }
```

`objective` is open text; the suggested set is awareness, acquisition, launch,
conversion, retention, event_promotion, custom.

## Deployments

`deployment_key` = `enroll_<enrollment-uuid>:<channel>:<format>:<slot-name>`,
UNIQUE per distribution and STABLE across replans — that is what makes launch,
resume, and reconciliation idempotent.

Desired vs observed are kept apart permanently:
- `status` (desired): `active` | `paused` | `canceled`
- `observed_status`: `pending` | `provisioning` | `live` | `paused` | `pending_review` | `rejected` | `failed` | `completed` | `unknown`

They disagree routinely; that is not an error. Persistent divergence fires
`deployment.drifted`.

Each partner deployment owns its OWN attribution instrument (ids land in
`external_ids`), distinct from the enrollment's evergreen `referral_code`.

`retrieve` additionally includes a `capabilities` descriptor honest to the
deployment's current state; `list` omits it. `list` filters by `distribution`.

## Operations

Every external mutation that does real work returns an Operation. It is never
"the response you were waiting for" — it is the handle you poll.

Statuses: `pending` `running` `waiting` `succeeded` `partial` `failed` `canceled`.
The last four are terminal. `partial` is a real outcome (some children
succeeded), not a transient state.

`waiting_reason` (a waiting op ALWAYS carries one): `funding_required`,
`provider_review`, `awaiting_target_settle`, `awaiting_children_settle`,
`awaiting_cleanup`. Waiting ops are woken by domain events when the blocker
settles, with a cron poller as the universal backstop.

```js
const operation = await boomin.operations.wait(id, { timeout: 120000, pollInterval: 2000 });
```

`wait()` resolves on ANY terminal status — inspect `operation.status` yourself.
It does NOT throw on a failed operation. It throws `BoominError` with code
`operation_wait_timeout` ONLY when your timeout elapses.

`operations:read` is granted to EVERY valid token implicitly.

`list` filters: `subjectType`, `subjectId` (prefixed id or bare uuid), `status`.

One live mutation per subject: a second launch/resume/apply raises
`operation_conflict` (409) — poll the live one instead. Cancel runs on a separate
CONTROL plane, so a cancel can coexist with the launch it targets.

Repeated `cancel()` on a subject with a live cancel is idempotent (returns the
existing control operation). A failed cancel with unresolved teardown keeps the
gate closed BY DESIGN -> `cancellation_requires_intervention` (409) carrying the
failed operation id; an operator retry resolves it. Competing mutations during a
live cancel get `cancellation_in_progress` (409).

Cancel teardown order: supersede the live launch -> stop new deployment creation
-> deployments desired=canceled -> adapter cleanup -> release the UNCONSUMED
budget remainder -> preserve `external_ids`, observed state, and cleanup failures.

## Budgets

`budget: { mode, asset, total }` — `mode` is `none` | `metered` | `funded`,
`asset` is `usd` | `credit`, `total` is MINOR UNITS. The serialized object also
carries live `consumed` and `released`.

- `funded` requires an asset and a positive total, else `budget_incomplete` at validate.
- Reservation happens AT LAUNCH, not at create: wallet available -> reserved, keyed on the distribution so a retried launch cannot double-reserve. Emits `budget.reserved`.
- Insufficient funds -> `budget.reserve_failed` + the operation parks at `waiting` / `funding_required`. Relaunching REUSES the waiting operation.
- Drawdown: each reward grant claims its amount exactly once, reserved -> pending.
- Release: the UNCONSUMED remainder returns to available on cancel or completion. Emits `budget.released`. Consumed budget stays consumed.
- `deployments[].budget_allocation_minor` carries a deployment's share when allocated.
- Value only enters the ledger at the platform boundary. There is no API call that mints money.

## Performance (measurement IN)

```js
await boomin.performance.events.create({
  deployment: "dep_...",           // required — everything hangs off the deployment
  type: "purchase",                // your vocabulary, <= 64 chars
  source: "checkout",              // optional, default "platform_api"
  occurred_at: "2026-08-01T12:00:00Z",
  value_minor: 4999,
  currency: "usd",
  quantity: 1,
  idempotency_key: "order_1001",   // 8-200 chars
  external_event_id: "shopify_1001",
  properties: { order_id: "1001" },
});
```

ONE of `idempotency_key` or `external_event_id` is REQUIRED, else
`performance_event_identity_required` (422). `idempotency_key` is unique per
(brand, source); `external_event_id` per (provider, source). 201 on first
ingestion, 200 with `duplicate: true` on replay. `projected: true` means the
event also projected into the program metric spine.

You never send a partner, enrollment, or program — that context is derived
through the deployment, which is why it cannot drift.

Reward eligibility is resolved at `occurred_at`, NOT at ingestion. Send a
truthful `occurred_at` when backfilling.

```js
const summary = await boomin.performance.summary({ distribution: "dist_..." });
// { object, filters, events, value_minor, by_type: [{ type, events, value_minor, quantity }] }
```

Both filters (`distribution`, `deployment`) are optional; with neither you get
the brand-wide rollup. `by_type` is ordered by event count descending.

## Events (operational feed OUT)

```js
for await (const event of boomin.events.list({ startingAfter: lastSeenSeq })) { }
```

Event shape (byte-identical to a webhook delivery):

```json
{
  "id": "evt_...", "object": "event", "type": "distribution.live", "seq": 48213,
  "subject": { "type": "distribution", "id": "…" }, "data": {},
  "operation": "op_...", "livemode": true, "created_at": "2026-08-02T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

`events.list` pages FORWARD by ascending `seq` (every other list pages backward
by creation time). `starting_after` accepts a seq NUMBER or an `evt_` id.

Public vocabulary — the registry IS the exposure boundary; unlisted types never
leave the org and are not addressable as a filter or a webhook subscription:

- distribution.launching, .live, .paused, .resumed, .completed, .failed, .canceled
- deployment.created, .activated, .rejected, .paused, .completed, .drifted, .cancel_requested, .canceled, .cleanup_failed
- partnership.created, .activated, .paused, .resumed, .ended
- enrollment.created, .approved, .rejected, .activated
- payout.created, .settled, .failed
- operation.succeeded, .failed, .cancel_requested, .canceled, .superseded
- budget.reserved, .released, .reserve_failed

Webhooks for reaction + a periodic `events.list` sweep from the last durably
stored `seq` is the production shape: it closes any delivery that exhausted its
retries.

## Webhooks

```js
const { webhook_endpoint } = await boomin.webhooks.endpoints.create({
  url: "https://your-app.com/webhooks/boomin",
  description: "Production",
  enabled_events: ["distribution.live", "payout.settled"],
});
console.log(webhook_endpoint.secret); // whsec_… — shown ONCE
```

- `https` required; plain `http` allowed for loopback (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]) only.
- Every `enabled_events` entry must be a public type, else `invalid_event_type` (400). Empty/omitted = ALL public types.
- The signing secret appears exactly twice in an endpoint's life: the create response and each rotate_secret response.
- NO history backfill: a new endpoint receives events appended at or after its creation. Close gaps with `events.list`.
- `update({ status: "disabled" })` stops delivery without destroying the endpoint or secret. A disabled endpoint exhausts in-flight deliveries immediately.
- `del()` is a hard delete; the idempotency cache is consulted BEFORE the row lookup, so a replayed DELETE returns the cached response instead of 404ing.

### Signature

```
Boomin-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex hmac>[,v1=<hex hmac>]
```

HMAC-SHA256 over `${t}.${rawBody}`, keyed by the endpoint secret. Multiple `v1`
entries appear during rotation.

```js
import { constructEvent } from "@boomin/sdk/webhooks";
// or Boomin.webhooks.constructEvent(...)

const event = await constructEvent(payload, sigHeader, secret, { tolerance: 300 });
```

THREE things to get right:
1. It is ASYNC (WebCrypto). Forgetting `await` gives a promise that never fails your check — the classic silent hole. Always `await` inside a try.
2. Pass the RAW body (string | Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer). Never JSON.parse and re-stringify — key order and whitespace change the bytes and the HMAC will not match.
3. Catch and reject: failure throws `WebhookSignatureVerificationError` (code `webhook_signature_invalid`).

Options: `tolerance` (default 300 seconds; 0 disables the age check), `now`
(override the clock, tests only). `secret` accepts a single string OR an array of
candidates.

Express: use `express.raw({ type: "application/json" })` for that route, not
`express.json`. Workers: `await request.text()` and hand the string over.

### Rotation

`rotateSecret` installs a fresh `whsec_…` and keeps the PREVIOUS secret honored
for a 24-HOUR overlap window. During the window every delivery carries TWO `v1`
entries — current first, previous second — so a receiver holding either verifies.

Zero-downtime: rotate and store the new secret alongside the old -> verify against
`[current, next]` for the length of the window -> after 24h promote and drop.

Rotating AGAIN inside the window replaces the previous secret; only the most
recent old secret is honored. Do not chain two rotations inside 24 hours.

### Delivery and retries

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Attempts | 6 total (1 initial + 5 retries) |
| Backoff after failure n | 30s -> 2m -> 8m -> 30m -> 30m |
| Per-attempt timeout | 10 seconds |
| Success | any 2xx |
| Ordering | NOT guaranteed — retries reorder |

Retries come from Boomin's own scheduler, not queue redelivery, and each attempt
is leased so a concurrent sweeper cannot double-send. After the sixth failed
attempt the delivery is terminal.

Consequences: answer 2xx FAST (a 10s timeout counts as failure — acknowledge
first, process asynchronously); be idempotent (dedupe on `event.id`); do not
depend on order (use `event.seq`).

## Payouts

```js
await boomin.payouts.run({ period_start: "2026-08-01", period_end: "2026-09-01" });
const batch = await boomin.payouts.exportCsv({ period_start: "2026-08-01", period_end: "2026-09-01" });
```

- `run` recomputes the period's rows (idempotent upsert). `period_start` must be strictly before `period_end`, else `invalid_period` (400). Batched rows are NEVER mutated by a re-run.
- Payout statuses: `pending` `awaiting_account` `processing` `paid` `failed`.
- Eligible for a batch = status `pending` or `awaiting_account` AND not brand-bridged (brand-bridged rows stay on the wallet rail — never both).
- `exportCsv` builds a `csv_batch` over eligible rows, exports it, and returns `download_url`. Answers 201. READ `skipped` — it names rows left out and why.
- Column maps for PayPal / Wise are per-brand config. The confirm and money-move steps are finance-gated and live in the app, not the Platform API.
- `connectStatus` returns configured rails plus `stripe: { configured, partner_accounts, partner_accounts_payouts_enabled }`. Check it BEFORE a run.
- `batches.list` returns every batch in one envelope (no pagination, `has_more` always false); `batches.retrieve` adds `items`.
- The `stripe_connect` rail disburses to partner Express accounts, keyed per payout item so a retry cannot double-send, with reversal on failure.

## Errors

```json
{ "error": { "code": "distribution_not_ready", "message": "…", "param": null, "request_id": "req_…" } }
```

SDK classes: `BoominError` (base: `code`, `status`, `requestId`, `param`, `raw`),
`AuthenticationError`, `PermissionError`, `InvalidRequestError`, `RateLimitError`,
`ConflictError`, `APIError`, plus promoted `OperationConflictError`,
`BandLimitReachedError`, `FundingRequiredError`,
`WebhookSignatureVerificationError`.

Class selection: first by typed `code`, then by HTTP status.
400/402/404/422 -> InvalidRequestError, 401 -> AuthenticationError,
403 -> PermissionError, 409 -> ConflictError, 429 -> RateLimitError,
else APIError. Promoted codes: `operation_conflict` and
`cancellation_in_progress` -> OperationConflictError, `band_limit_reached` ->
BandLimitReachedError, `funding_required` -> FundingRequiredError.

Retries: the SDK retries 429 and 5xx up to `maxRetries` (default 2) with jittered
exponential backoff, honouring `Retry-After`. Mutations are safe to retry because
they always carry an `Idempotency-Key`. Connection errors and timeouts retry too;
other 4xx never do.

Key codes and recovery:
- `platform_token_required` (401) — no Bearer header. v1 is Bearer-only.
- `platform_token_unknown` / `_inactive` / `_expired` / `_org_missing` (401) — mint or rotate a key.
- `missing_scope` (403) — message is `missing_scope:<scope>`. Mint a key with that scope.
- `band_limit_reached` (402) — the org's active-partner band is full. Upgrade the band.
- `operation_conflict` (409) — a live operation holds the subject's concurrency slot. Retrieve and poll it; do not enqueue a rival.
- `cancellation_in_progress` (409) — a cancel holds the control gate. Wait for it to settle.
- `cancellation_requires_intervention` (409) — a previous cancel failed with unresolved teardown; the gate stays closed by design. Carries the failed operation id; an operator retry resolves it.
- `channel_type_not_yet_supported` (422) — no adapter for that slot. Surfaced by validate() before launch.
- `performance_event_identity_required` (422) — send `idempotency_key` or `external_event_id`.
- `idempotency_key_conflict` (409) — same key, different body. Use a fresh key.
- `invalid_cursor` / `invalid_status` / `invalid_event_type` / `invalid_period` / `invalid_request` (400).
- `create_rate_limit_exceeded` (429) — back off and retry.
- Lifecycle 409s: `distribution_not_editable`, `distribution_programs_draft_only`, `distribution_not_validatable`, `distribution_not_ready`, `distribution_not_pausable|_resumable|_cancelable`, `deployment_not_pausable|_resumable|_cancelable`, `enrollment_not_pausable|_resumable`, `partnership_not_pausable|_resumable|_endable`, `connection_not_revocable`.
- `test_mode_not_yet_available` (400) — `sk_test_`/`pk_test_` are reserved but not built.
- `developer_access_paused` (503) — operator kill switch. Retry later.
- 404s (`distribution_not_found`, `deployment_not_found`, `enrollment_not_found`, `partnership_not_found`, `connection_not_found`, `operation_not_found`, `program_not_found`, `partner_not_found`, `payout_batch_not_found`, `webhook_endpoint_not_found`, `brand_not_found`) are returned identically for "does not exist", "belongs to another org", and "malformed id". Existence is never leaked across tenants.

`funding_required` is primarily an operation `waiting_reason`, not a terminal
error: a funded launch with an underfunded wallet PARKS and resumes once topped
up. `FundingRequiredError` exists for surfaces that raise it synchronously.

SDK-local codes (raised by the client, never the API): `operation_wait_timeout`,
`webhook_signature_invalid`, `request_timeout`, `connection_error`,
`internal_error`.

## Providers are internal adapters

Instagram, TikTok, Meta Ads and the rest NEVER appear in the public API as a
resource, a parameter, or a route. You express intent through the deployment
plan's `mode` / `medium` / `channel` / `format` and the registry resolves an
adapter — or rejects the combination during `validate()` with
`channel_type_not_yet_supported`.

Exactly ONE adapter is registered today: the Boomin partnership adapter,
supporting `partner` / `referral` / `boomin` / `referral_link`. Everything else
fails validation rather than failing at launch.

## Connections

Connection = a provider identity owned by a partner XOR a brand
(`kind`: social_profile | ad_account | page | pixel | payout). A grant is one
partnership's right to use it.

Visible to your token when your brand owns it OR a live grant reaches it through
one of your partnerships; anything else is `connection_not_found`.

`revoke()`: brand-owned -> the connection itself is revoked; partner-owned -> only
YOUR grants are revoked (the identity is the partner's). Already-revoked ->
`connection_not_revocable` (409).

## Partner Connect (browser)

```bash
npm install @boomin/connect
npx @boomin/cli init
```

`npx @boomin/cli init` opens a browser login/signup flow, lets the developer
select or create a Boomin organization and program, ensures a Partner Connect
config exists, appends localhost origins, and writes `.env.local`:

```env
VITE_BOOMIN_PUBLIC_KEY=pk_live_...
VITE_BOOMIN_PROGRAM_ID=...
VITE_BOOMIN_API_BASE=https://api.boomin.ai/v1/connect
```

```js
import Boomin from "@boomin/connect";

Boomin.init({
  publicKey: import.meta.env.VITE_BOOMIN_PUBLIC_KEY,
  programId: import.meta.env.VITE_BOOMIN_PROGRAM_ID,
  apiBase: import.meta.env.VITE_BOOMIN_API_BASE,
  redirectUri: window.location.origin + window.location.pathname,
});

await Boomin.requestOtp({ email: "creator@example.com", name: "Creator" });
await Boomin.verifyOtp({ email: "creator@example.com", code: "123456" });
await Boomin.connectInstagram({ requireCreator: true });
```

After redirect:

```js
const result = Boomin.consumeRedirectResult();
if (result?.sessionId) {
  const status = await Boomin.getConnectStatus(result.sessionId);
}
```

Surface configuration is readable and writable from the Platform API via
`programs.connectConfig` (scopes `connect_config:read` / `:write`):
`public_key`, `allowed_origins`, `allowed_redirect_origins`,
`required_channels`, `default_approval_status` (pending | approved).

## Signed Handoff

Use Signed Handoff when the customer app already has a logged-in user, so the
partner does not enter a second email OTP.

```bash
npm install @boomin/server
npx @boomin/cli handoff init --framework next --auth custom
npx @boomin/cli handoff provision
```

```js
import { createBoominCreatorJoinHandler } from "@boomin/server/next";

export const GET = createBoominCreatorJoinHandler({
  publicKey: process.env.BOOMIN_CONNECT_PUBLIC_KEY,
  programId: process.env.BOOMIN_CONNECT_PROGRAM_ID,
  redirectUri: process.env.BOOMIN_CONNECT_REDIRECT_URI,
  signingSecret: process.env.BOOMIN_HANDOFF_SIGNING_SECRET,
  issuer: "your-app.com",
  loginUrl: "/login",
  getCurrentUser: async (request) => ({
    externalUserId: "user_123",
    email: "creator@example.com",
    name: "Creator",
    metadata: {},
  }),
});
```

Handoff payloads are HMAC-SHA256 signed stable JSON, expire quickly, use one-time
nonces, and must target an allowed redirect origin.

Issuer configuration is managed from the Platform API via
`programs.handoffConfig` (scopes `handoff:read` / `:write`) — create-or-update
per issuer, filterable by `?issuer=`. The `hs_boomin_live_…` signing secret is
returned ONLY when just minted or explicitly supplied.

`@boomin/server` is MAINTENANCE ONLY — it exists for these generated routes.
Server work against the Platform API uses `@boomin/sdk`.

## Referral-first install path

```bash
npx @boomin/cli init
npx @boomin/cli referral init --framework next --auth custom --write
npx @boomin/cli handoff provision
npx @boomin/cli doctor
```

`init --list` (or answering yes to the interactive prompt) lists the program on
the public Discover feed; the default is private. With `--auth custom`, wire the
generated `getCurrentUser` to your auth; `clerk` and `supabase` are prewired.
`handoff provision --rotate` invalidates the old secret.

The join call creates the partner, the enrollment, and the referral code; clicks
on `/r/CODE` are tracked as link clicks in standing metrics.

Generated files:
- `app/api/boomin/partner/join/route.js` signs the current app user into Boomin.
- `app/api/boomin/partner/status/route.js` fetches only the current user's standing.
- `app/r/[code]/route.js` records `link_clicks` and redirects with `?ref=<code>`.
- `app/partner/page.jsx` shows referral link, copy button, metrics, approval, qualification, and optional Instagram connect.

Standing response:

```json
{
  "referral": { "code": "ABC123", "url": "https://app.example/r/ABC123", "active": true },
  "metrics": { "linkClicks": 0, "signups": 0, "sales": 0, "gmvCents": 0, "productUsage": 0 },
  "approvalStatus": "pending",
  "qualificationStatus": "qualified",
  "requiredChannels": [],
  "missingChannels": []
}
```

Instagram is optional. Referral-only programs use `requiredChannels: []`.
Programs requiring Instagram return referral data plus
`missingChannels: ["instagram"]` until OAuth completes.

## Qualification

`programs.requirements` fields: `scope` (program_entry | program_maintenance |
tier | campaign | benefit | invite), `scope_id`, `metric_key`, `operator`
(gte | lte | eq | neq | exists), `threshold`, `window_days` (null = lifetime),
`source`, `weight`, `required`, `status` (active | paused | archived).

Closed metric vocabulary: `followers`, `views`, `post_count`, `collab_posts`,
`link_clicks`, `referral_count`, `gmv_cents`, `sales_count`,
`product_usage_count`, `channel_connected`, `manual_approval`,
`event_registration`, `template_install`. Anything else is `invalid_request`.

Deleting a requirement ARCHIVES it and re-evaluates the program.
`programs.tiers` are keyed by `rank` — creating at an existing rank upserts;
lists come back ordered by ascending rank.

## CLI 0.3.0

Setup: `login`, `logout`, `status`, `doctor`, `init`.
Keys: `token create|list|revoke|rotate`, `scopes`, `scopes explain <scope>`.
Scaffolding: `referral init`, `handoff init|provision`, `mcp install`, `skill install`.
Smoke: `platform smoke --read-only | --write --cleanup | --all-scopes --cleanup`.

Platform v1 groups over the live REST tree:

```bash
npx @boomin/cli distribution create|list|get|validate|launch|pause|resume|cancel
npx @boomin/cli enrollment invite|approve|reject|list|get
npx @boomin/cli partnership list|get|pause|resume|end
npx @boomin/cli connection list|get|revoke
npx @boomin/cli payout list|run|export|connect
npx @boomin/cli webhook create|list|delete|rotate-secret
npx @boomin/cli events list --type <event.type>
```

Operation-returning commands (launch/pause/resume/cancel) POLL THE OPERATION TO A
TERMINAL STATUS BY DEFAULT; `--no-wait` returns the 202 immediately.
`--timeout <seconds>` defaults to 120, `--poll-interval <secs>` to 2.

`distribution create` flags: `--name` (required), `--objective`, `--programs`
(csv), `--description`, `--spec <json>`, `--budget <json>` or
`--budget-mode/--budget-asset/--budget-total`.

Auth: `--token sk_boomin_live_...`, `BOOMIN_PLATFORM_TOKEN`, or saved config.
`--brand <id-or-slug>` sets the `Boomin-Brand` header. `--json` everywhere.

Global flags: `-h/--help`, `--json`, `--api-base`, `--platform-api-base`,
`--web-base`, `--connect-api-base`.

On a scope failure the CLI prints the typed code, the required scope, and a
ready-to-run `token create` fix.

```bash
npx @boomin/cli platform smoke --read-only --token sk_boomin_live_...
npx @boomin/cli platform smoke --write --cleanup --token sk_boomin_live_...
npx @boomin/cli platform smoke --all-scopes --cleanup --json
```

`platform smoke --all-scopes` creates a temporary all-scope token if none is
supplied, executes all registered V1 scopes through `POST /scopes_exec` on
`https://api.boomin.ai/v1/platform`, cleans up created smoke objects with
`--cleanup`, and revokes the temporary token.

## Boomin MCP

```bash
npx @boomin/cli@latest skill install
npx @boomin/cli@latest mcp install
npx @boomin/cli@latest doctor
```

Restart Claude Code or Codex after install so the Boomin skill metadata and MCP
server are loaded.

Manual hosted install:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http boomin https://mcp.boomin.ai/mcp
```

OAuth-aware MCP clients can connect directly to `https://mcp.boomin.ai/mcp`.
Missing or expired authorization returns a standards-style OAuth challenge
pointing clients to `https://mcp.boomin.ai/authorize`.

The CLI `mcp install` path creates a scoped platform token and writes it into
Claude Code's user MCP config as a static bearer header. OAuth-aware clients can
use the hosted consent flow instead. Both paths map to Boomin platform scopes and
audit logs.

Default skill pack — `Referral Program Installer`: `boomin.doctor`,
`boomin.detect_project`, `boomin.get_connect_config`,
`boomin.scaffold_referral_first`, `boomin.verify_referral_install`,
`boomin.get_partner_standing`, `boomin.record_test_event`.

Admin opt-in skill pack — `Program Operator`: `boomin.get_program`,
`boomin.update_program`, `boomin.update_required_channels`,
`boomin.update_referral_settings`, requirement CRUD, tier CRUD, program
evaluation. Requires explicit scopes such as `programs:update`,
`connect_config:write`, `program_requirements:write`, `program_tiers:write`.

## Public vs private credentials

Public Partner Connect key:
- Prefix: `pk_live_...`
- Browser-safe.
- Starts OTP and Instagram Partner Connect flows.
- Restricted by allowed origins and redirect origins.

Private platform key:
- Prefix: `sk_boomin_live_...`
- Server/agent only. NEVER in browser code, mobile bundles, or public repos.
- Scoped, revocable, audited, idempotent.
- Create endpoints limited to 150 creates/hour per org + token + resource family.

Test mode: `sk_test_` / `pk_test_` are RESERVED and answer
`test_mode_not_yet_available`. Every object already carries `livemode`, so full
test mode will need no backfill. Until then: a disposable brand with live keys,
plus `validate()` as the pre-launch dry run.

## Key management

```bash
npx @boomin/cli token create --name "Server" --scopes org:read,distributions:read --save
npx @boomin/cli token list --json
npx @boomin/cli token revoke <token_id>
npx @boomin/cli token rotate <token_id> --save
```

The secret is shown ONCE on create and rotate. Rotation revokes the old key and
creates a replacement with the same scope set. Revoked keys return 401.

## V1 scopes

Distribution core: `org:read`, `distributions:read`, `distributions:write`,
`distributions:launch`, `deployments:read`, `performance:read`,
`performance:write`, `operations:read` (IMPLICITLY GRANTED to every valid token),
`events:read`, `payouts:read`, `payouts:write`.

Relationships: `partnerships:read|write`, `enrollments:read|write`,
`connections:read|write`, `partners:read`.

Programs: `programs:read|create|update|delete`,
`program_requirements:read|write`, `program_tiers:read|write`,
`program_resources:read|write`, `connect_config:read|write`,
`handoff:read|write`, `campaigns:read|write`, `benefits:read|write`,
`webhooks:read|write`.

Content: `series:read|create|update|delete`,
`units:read|create|update|delete|publish`.

UI and assets: `pages:read|write|delete`, `canvas:read|write|delete`,
`files:read|write|delete`.

Automation and data: `agents:read|write|run`, `workflows:read|write|run`,
`contacts:read`, `segments:read|write`, `events:write`.

Commerce: `commerce:read`, `commerce:write` (excludes billing and payouts).

Legacy `program_members:read` and `program_members:approve` are accepted as
aliases for the enrollment scopes on already-issued tokens.

`distributions:launch` is deliberately separate from `distributions:write`:
spending money is not the same permission as editing a draft.
`performance:write` (ingestion IN) is deliberately distinct from `events:read`
(operational feed OUT). Mutating a deployment requires `distributions:write` —
`deployments:read` is a read-only grant by design.

## Discover feed and hosted surfaces

- `GET https://api.boomin.ai/v1/connect/discover` — public, unauthenticated feed of listed programs (display-safe program cards + requirements summary; offset-paginated, limit max 50).
- Partners browse and apply at `boomin.ai/connect`, then track applications and referral links there. A Partners tab appears in a partner's workspace once a program approves them.
- Brands operate programs at `boomin.ai` under Partners: active partners + views this month, member table with OAuth-verified socials, applications inbox (approve/reject), and a "List on Connect discover" toggle.

## Pricing

Billed on monthly ACTIVE partners only: a partner is active in a calendar month
when they are approved AND drove >=1 tracked event (referral-link click or
tracked post) that month. Dormant partners are always free. A partner in two
programs counts ONCE — the aggregation key is the distinct partnership.

Tiers: Free up to 10 active, Starter $79/mo up to 25, Growth $299/mo up to 100,
Scale $999/mo up to 500, beyond that contact. Views are never billed — they are
OAuth-verified value metrics, not billing metrics.

Neither enrollment pause nor partnership pause affects billability: links keep
resolving under both, so pausing never dodges fees. Archive or
`partnership.end` are the billing exits.

## Deprecated

- `boominjs` — DEPRECATED. Use `@boomin/sdk` for the Platform API, or `@boomin/connect` for browser Partner Connect.
- `@boomin/server` — MAINTENANCE ONLY, for the generated Signed Handoff routes.
- "Creator Connect" is the former name of Partner Connect. Old `/creator-connect/*` doc paths 301 to `/partner-connect/*`.
- The pre-v1 RPC routes under `/v1/platform` remain functional for CLI 0.2.0, MCP, and existing integrations. New work uses the REST tree and `@boomin/sdk`.

## OpenAPI

Partner Connect:
- Docs: https://developers.boomin.ai/api/connect/
- Spec: https://developers.boomin.ai/openapi/connect.yaml

Platform API:
- Docs: https://developers.boomin.ai/api/platform/
- Spec: https://developers.boomin.ai/openapi/platform.yaml

## Product principle

Distribution is intent; deployments are execution; performance is measurement.
Programs stay durable — a distribution runs THROUGH a program, never instead of
one. Providers are internal adapters and never become public API surface.
